questions.stem: The highest court in Nigeria's judicial hierarchy is the
questions.explanation: The Supreme Court is the final appellate court, so no appeal lies from its decisions. It also has original jurisdiction in disputes between the Federation and a state or between states.

distractorRationale.a: The Court of Appeal sits immediately below the Supreme Court and its decisions may be appealed further
distractorRationale.b: The Federal High Court is a court of first instance in the third level of the hierarchy
distractorRationale.d: The National Industrial Court has specialised jurisdiction over labour and employment matters

sources.title: Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria 1999 (as amended), section 230

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a function of the judiciary?

options.text: Interpreting the provisions of the Constitution
Protecting the fundamental rights of citizens
Preparing the annual budget of the Federation
Settling disputes between two state governments

questions.explanation: Preparing budget estimates is an executive function, later authorised by the legislature. The judiciary neither raises nor allocates public revenue; it adjudicates.

distractorRationale.a: Constitutional interpretation is a core judicial function
distractorRationale.b: Enforcing Chapter IV rights is expressly a judicial task
distractorRationale.d: Interstate disputes fall within the Supreme Court's original jurisdiction

questions.stem: A boundary dispute between two Nigerian states should be filed in the first instance before the

options.text: High Court of one of the states concerned

questions.explanation: The Constitution gives the Supreme Court original jurisdiction in disputes between states, and between the Federation and a state. Referring such a case to the court of one of the parties would compromise its impartiality, which is precisely why the Constitution sends it straight to the top.

distractorRationale.a: A state High Court cannot sit in judgment over a dispute involving its own state as a party
distractorRationale.b: The Court of Appeal is essentially appellate, with limited first-instance jurisdiction over presidential election petitions
distractorRationale.d: The Federal High Court hears federal revenue, admiralty and similar matters, not interstate disputes

sources.title: Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria 1999 (as amended), section 232

questions.stem: Which of the following most directly protects the independence of the Nigerian judiciary?

options.text: Security of tenure, with judges holding office until a fixed retirement age
The appointment of judges by state governors alone
The publication of judgments in newspapers
Annual negotiation of judicial salaries with the executive

questions.explanation: A judge who cannot be dismissed for an unpopular ruling can decide against the government without risking his livelihood. Nigeria fixes retirement at 70 for Justices of the Supreme Court and Court of Appeal and at 65 for other judicial officers.

distractorRationale.b: Unilateral political appointment would increase, not reduce, executive influence; the National Judicial Council exists to check it
distractorRationale.c: Publicity aids transparency but does not secure a judge's position
distractorRationale.d: Annual negotiation would give the executive recurring leverage, which is why salaries are a first-line charge on the Consolidated Revenue Fund

sources.title: Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria 1999 (as amended), sections 84 and 291

questions.stem: The body that recommends the appointment and discipline of judicial officers in Nigeria is the
questions.explanation: The National Judicial Council, chaired by the Chief Justice of Nigeria, recommends candidates for judicial appointment and handles the discipline and removal of judges. Placing these powers in a judicial body rather than a political one is a key safeguard of independence.

distractorRationale.a: The Nigerian Bar Association is a professional association of lawyers, not a constitutional appointing body
distractorRationale.c: The Federal Character Commission monitors the equitable spread of appointments across states
distractorRationale.d: The Council of State is an advisory body of past and present leaders with a different mandate

sources.title: Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria 1999 (as amended), Third Schedule Part I

questions.stem: Ouster clauses inserted in military decrees undermined the Nigerian judiciary because they

options.text: increased the number of judges on the Supreme Court
barred the courts from inquiring into the validity of those decrees
required all cases to be heard by juries
transferred judicial powers to state legislatures

questions.explanation: An ouster clause expressly removed the jurisdiction of the courts over a decree, so however clearly a decree violated rights no judge could examine it. This destroyed judicial review, which is the judiciary's principal check on the other organs.

distractorRationale.a: The size of the Supreme Court is a matter of constitutional composition, unrelated to ouster clauses
distractorRationale.c: Jury trial was not the mechanism at issue in military decrees
distractorRationale.d: Legislatures were dissolved under military rule, so nothing was transferred to them

questions.stem: Through the doctrine of binding precedent, decisions of Nigeria's higher courts effectively develop the law.
questions.explanation: True. Once the Supreme Court settles the meaning of a provision, lower courts must follow that interpretation, so the ruling becomes part of the law in practice. This quasi-legislative effect is one of the recognised limitations on strict separation of powers.

distractorRationale.b: This assumes courts only apply pre-existing rules, which ignores how judicial interpretation fills gaps and resolves ambiguity

questions.stem: An appeal against the judgment of a State High Court in a civil case goes to the
questions.explanation: Appeals move upward one level at a time, and the Court of Appeal sits immediately above the High Courts. Only after the Court of Appeal has ruled can the matter reach the Supreme Court.

distractorRationale.a: The Supreme Court hears appeals from the Court of Appeal, not directly from a High Court
distractorRationale.c: The Federal High Court is a court of coordinate level with a State High Court, so it cannot hear its appeals
distractorRationale.d: The Customary Court of Appeal hears appeals on customary law from customary courts, not from a State High Court

sources.title: Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria 1999 (as amended), section 240
